    Standard error of the log odds ratio, binary predictor

    se_binary_po.Rd

    Computes the standard error (and confidence interval) of the log odds ratio for a binary (e.g. treatment) predictor in a proportional-odds model, at a given total sample size n.

    se_binary_po(
  pc,
  OR = NULL,
  pe = NULL,
  rr = NULL,
  n,
  r = 1,
  method = c("ologit", "whitehead"),
  conf = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    pc

    Control-arm category probabilities (sum to 1).

    OR, pe, rr

    Exactly one, defining the experimental arm; see build_arm_probs().

    n

    Total sample size (both arms).

    r

    Allocation ratio, treatment:control.

    method

    "ologit" (default; exact MLE) or "whitehead" (delta-method approximation).

    conf

    Confidence level for the reported interval.

    Value

    A list with elements OR, conf, SE (of the log OR), lower, upper (CI limits for the OR), and method.

    Details

    Two approaches to the SE are supported, selectable via method:

    • "whitehead" - Whitehead's (1993) delta-method variance approximation (fast, closed-form; assumes proportional odds and can be inaccurate for large effects).

    • "ologit" - White, Marley-Zagar, Morris, Parmar, Royston & Babiker (2023) fit a weighted proportional-odds model directly to the anticipated distribution and read the SE off the observed information matrix. This is exact (no delta-method approximation): the SE is computed from a fit at the anticipated (alternative) arm-level probabilities, i.e. their "SA" variant, since trial data actually arise under (approximately) the planning effect, not under a null effect.

    "whitehead" and "ologit" nearly coincide for small effects and diverge as the anticipated effect grows, which is White et al.'s stated motivation for preferring the exact "ologit" fit for large effects.

    Examples

    pc <- c(0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.45)
se_binary_po(pc, OR = 1.7, n = 30, method = "whitehead")
#> $OR
#> [1] 1.7
#> 
#> $conf
#> [1] 0.95
#> 
#> $SE
#> [1] 0.6557662
#> 
#> $lower
#> [1] 0.4701752
#> 
#> $upper
#> [1] 6.146645
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "whitehead"
#> 
se_binary_po(pc, OR = 1.7, n = 30, method = "ologit")
#> $OR
#> [1] 1.7
#> 
#> $conf
#> [1] 0.95
#> 
#> $SE
#> [1] 0.6613742
#> 
#> $lower
#> [1] 0.4650356
#> 
#> $upper
#> [1] 6.214578
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "ologit"
#>
